text: The furnace is still the furnace.
why: Internal/abstract shorthand escaping into player prose.

text: Eight hundred dollars arrives that nothing is already claiming.
why: Unnatural abstract wording; money framed from the ledger's viewpoint.

text: Something decided earlier...
why: Internal state/label leakage.

text: The half of the week you agreed to hold.
why: System-state phrasing leaking into narrative.

text: The thing... / the week... / something...
why: Vague pointer where the concrete referent is available.

text: Money is tight at home.
why: Asserts knowledge the character has not actually acquired.

text: Vote no and risk angering leadership.
why: Uncertain predicted consequence attached to a choice label.

text: Against your instincts, you keep your voice down.
why: Trait-driven internal narration overriding the player's explicit choice.

text: [artificially childlike wording because the character is young]
why: Age operates through knowledge, capability, authority, and noticed detail — never diction.

text: [dramatic payoff for every traced memory, repaid favor, or minor event]
why: Importance must be canonical, not engine-causal.

text: At 9:07, your phone rings. It's your mom.
why: Cinematic suspense by default for a serious event (a death); owner prefers grounded directness.

text: Don't answer.
why: Collapses politically meaningful behavior — silence vs. evasion are distinct actions when the distinction matters.

text: Marcus, your friend and caucus leader, asks you for the vote.
why: Repeated relationship re-explanation for an established recurring character.

text: A month later. / School continued... / The house went on...
why: Mechanical or synonym-cycled transitions; NO PROSE is often the right treatment.

text: You've been knocking doors for three hours.
why: Campaign-insider jargon as default narrative register; legal only in professional dialogue.

text: This reminds you of...
why: Prose forced to explain a causal connection merely because the engine can trace it.

text: The judge reads the motion again before the hearing.
why: Third-person narration of the player in a player-facing scene. The packet's CHARACTER role noun is who the player is, not a way to refer to them.

text: He gets to the office before his staff does.
why: Same POV failure in pronoun form; turns a played scene into a dossier about someone else.

text: You're a second-term state representative.
why: Restates stable character state the player already knows; orienting preamble instead of the scene.

text: HB 214 — your bill — comes up Thursday.
why: The designation is right; '— your bill —' is a redundant player-state reminder. 'HB 214 comes up Thursday.'

text: your spouse of eighteen years
why: Dossier exposition of an established relationship the player has lived in; label the person the way the player would.

text: It changes the shape of the conversation.
why: Literary abstraction about the conversation itself; say what actually changed — the pressure, the count, the dynamics.

text: You could say the plain thing.
why: Writerly gesture at directness instead of directness; if there is a plain thing to say, say it.

text: You stand there, holding the sentence.
why: Conspicuously literary image; narrate the observable action or end the scene.

text: That is not the version Aaron just put in the room.
why: Awkward generated metaphor; state what Aaron said and how it differs from the earlier account.

text: the one you've met exactly once
why: Unnatural precision used as characterization; reads generated. Refer to the person as the player would.

text: The offer: $500.
why: Game-show / abstract UI money label. Money is an arrangement: who pays, for what, on what terms.

text: [a closing sentence explaining what the moment will cost the player politically]
why: Interprets the scene more deterministically than the facts support; state the circumstance and let the player infer.

text: [continuing to narrate after the decision pressure has landed]
why: Delays returning control; a scene ends when the player can act.

text: [rewriting an approved rendering into one canonical sentence per packet, or re-varying it by synonym swap]
why: Several grounded renderings can all be right; variation comes from fact selection and ordering, never from synonym churn.
